page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical execution cores via multithreading on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio, paired with 32 MB of shared L3 cache and support for modern instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators.

Storage configuration on the L4as_v4 features 960 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, providing direct low-latency disk access for data-heavy applications. The platform does not incorporate discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking topologies or external IP allocation.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 2079.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3077.78. Multi-core performance aligns with expected dual-core physical limits, registering 6153.87 in stress-ng and 4766.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. While text processing and compression metrics perform reliably, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (36.89 GB/sec) and database operation throughput show lower comparative efficiency under high memory load.

Resource allocation provides a cost-efficient balance of localized NVMe disk density and dedicated compute capacity for smaller-scale transactional storage. The instance fits high-speed temporary caching, transactional logging, local file indexing, intermediate ETL stages, and localized database workloads where raw NVMe IOPS take priority over high thread counts.

With its 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio and bundled fast NVMe capacity, the instance delivers a balanced hardware profile for localized databases, caching layers, and search index nodes.
